# Storyboard: Chapter 12, A Spark at the Hedge

*Generated by `tools/storyboard.mjs` from `app/story/ch12.js`. Do not edit by hand: change the story file and run `node tools/storyboard.mjs` again.*

## How to read this

Every screen of the game is one comic panel, called a frame. Frames are listed in reading order. Each one has:

- **Shot**: the storyboard, written for an illustrator (camera, who is where, what the moment feels like, where the lettering goes).
- **Scene**: what the game draws today, in plain words: the set, the camera, who is in shot and how, and any effects.
- **Captions**: the narration boxes, read first. **Balloons**: who speaks, in order. **Sound effect**: the big lettering. A line marked *(only if …)* shows only to a reader whose choices match.
- **Then**: what the reader does next (tap Next, choose, type, pick a look, count by twos, or do a Counts lesson or a take-away lesson).

Where the reader makes a choice, each option’s frames are grouped under a **Branch** heading, and the branches meet again at the frame named after them. `{name}` is the first part of her Clan name (Moon makes Moonpaw), `{petname}` is what her Tall One calls her, and `{they}`/`{them}`/`{their}` become she/her/her or he/him/his. `{Murmur}`/`{murmur}` is the tortoiseshell’s name word: Murmur (Murmurpaw, Murmurchime, murmuring), or Mutter for a reader whose own Clan name is Murmur. `{ending}` is her warrior ending, `paw` until the Ceremony (Fernpaw, then Fernheart).

### f001 · panel 1

**Shot.** CLOSE-UP, THE TITLE PANEL, NOON. Our cat sleeps curled tight in its new warrior’s nest, bright noon light falling across the moss, its bark, its glass and the grey mist stone tucked round it; the next nest at the edge of the panel is empty. One small zzz rises. The chapter’s title is lettered across the top of the panel like a title page.

**Scene.** Den: the apprentices’ den under an enormous rosebush, in the morning. Camera: close on one nest (`nest`). Cast: you (curled up, sleepy, in the nest, facing left, eyes shut: asleep). Also: clear weather; Riffle’s lucky stone in her nest, right where she put it (by her nose or under her chin, as she chose); her Case File along the mossy edge of her nest: a piece of bark for each card she holds, overlapping like roof tiles; her secret cards under the moss, a corner showing for each; her piece of glass in its leaf, tucked under the moss beside the corners of bark: the leaf’s tip and one small glint showing; a second nest at the left edge of the close-up, a plain moss ring partly cut off by the panel’s edge (the next nest, with the warriors); her own nest a little to its right, with everything on it; the mist stone on the moss of her nest, beside her glass in its leaf and the corners of her secret bark: a smooth grey pebble, egg-shaped, the size of her paw. Effects: morning light, washed clean after the storm, sleepy zzz.

**Captions**

> Chapter 12: A Spark at the Hedge

(Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty!). 5 taps, her own two forepaws patted down together each time (they glow; a tap anywhere else makes them wiggle), each lighting all ten claws and putting the next number in Chispapaw’s balloon, out loud, in Spanish words lettered in italics (“Diez…”, then “Diez, veinte…” …); Read to me says each number in the Spanish voice (with none, in English). ## The Case File’s cards

A piece of bark for each thing she finds out: one picture scratched in, one line, and a mark in a corner (an eye for what she saw herself, an ear for what she was only told). Each goes into her Case File at the panel that gives it, in this order:

| Card | Mark | Its line | Given at | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## The book page

Title: *{name}{ending}’s First Frost-Time*. This chapter’s page, under “Chapter 12: A Spark at the Hedge”. Lines shown when their condition matches the reader’s choices:

- (always) On {name}{ending}’s first day as a warrior, {they} slept till noon, and Glintstar gave {them} a frost-time job: counting a new store under the Old Bridge, five hundred pieces by the full moon.
- (always) At the hedge, a little pillow cat from {their} old tower was counting the Clan in Spanish, the way {name}{ending} once watched through the glass.
- (always) {name}{ending} spoke up for her, and the little cat chose her own Clan name: Chispa, which means spark. Glintstar named her Chispapaw, and gave her to {name}{ending} as {their} very first apprentice.
- (always) In the Training Hollow, Tallyheart taught them both something new: take-aways, with loose ones, rows and squares, ones first.
- (always) At sunset the Clan’s first frost-time catch went into the store, and {name}{ending} counted what stayed: one hundred thirty-three, one square, three rows and three loose.
- (always) Riffle brought news: Granny has found another badger track, a fresh one.
- (always) At bedtime, Chispapaw did the paw thing in Spanish, all the way to fifty, and the grey tom snored.
- (no dream typed) {name}{ending}’s first frost-time dream stayed a secret.

**In the store:** under the recap, small, the store picture of 133 (one square, three rows and three loose), with “In the store:” in Comic Neue and 133 in Andika; it prints with the page.
